original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-strict-morphism-thickenings}
In Situation \ref{situation-morphism-thickenings} the morphism $(f, f')$
is a strict morphism of thickenings if and only if
(\ref{equation-morphism-thickenings}) is cartesian in the category
of ringed spaces.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

A morphism of first-order thickenings $(f,f')$ is a commuting square of ringed spaces $(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{i}(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{t}(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, with vertical morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal O_S)$. The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

For the commutative square of ringed-space thickenings above the morphism $(f, f')$
is a strict morphism of thickenings if and only if
that commuting square is cartesian in the category
of ringed spaces.
stage_b_review_note: The original strict-thickening criterion is precisely strictness of the morphism of first-order ringed-space thickenings iff the defining commutative square is cartesian as ringed spaces. The added kernel map f*J→I describes strictness and preserves the iff.
